title: manuscript-guard reference currency
description: literature/currency.yaml: for a sentence of the manuscript and one work it cites, whether the work is still the one to cite. Each entry is matched to the manuscript by the sentence's words, folded as a passage's are, and the citation key. Its decision is the rules' (`by: rules`, from two readings filed with `references --reading`) or a person's, with the reason; a proposed change waits for a person's answer. An entry of kind `novelty` is a claim of novelty or absence held to a recorded search for the earlier study: it names no work, holds every sentence that makes the claim, and has no decision and no answer.

work.description: A work by its DOI, in lower case, or its PMID: doi:10.1000/xyz or pmid:12345.

id.description: The entry's own id, which never changes: c1, c2 ...

kind.description: `currency` (the default): a citing sentence and one work it cites, and whether the work is still the one to cite. `novelty`: a claim of novelty or absence, held to a recorded search for the earlier study.

sentence.description: The citing sentence as the manuscript writes it. Its citations, case, line breaks and typography are folded before it is matched.

also.description: For a `novelty` entry: further sentences that make the same claim, each matched by its folded words as `sentence` is. One search answers them all.

question.description: The claim written as a question (rule F1).

not_a_claim.description: For a `novelty` entry: a person's word that the sentence makes no claim about the literature, with why. Never a model's.

by.description: `rules`, where the rules decided from the readings; else the person who decided, with `why`.
The person who answered: never `rules`, which decide and do not answer.

reply.description: Where the refusal is a reply in Word to the proposal's comment: its number under literature/currency/replies/. `why` is then the reply's words, and `by` its author as authors.yaml names them.

assessed_by.description: Who read the reply as a refusal (`references --assess`).
